transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-12
Start time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (NovaBank Head of ML), Emily Zhang (NovaBank Platform Eng), Rajiv Patel (NovaBank Director Eng)
Artifacts: Redwood Optimize deck (link), cost-model.xlsx (link), redwood-soc2.pdf (link), pilot-sow-draft.docx (link)

Summary:
Quick Optimize walkthrough focused on batching and prefix / KV cache recommendations and a live cost model. Customer cares about p95 latency <= 300ms for short query flows, strong data residency and KMS requirements, and predictable unit economics for a pilot. Redwood suggested batching window 8-16 for their workload, aggressive KV prefix caching for session-based flows, and a pilot to validate cache hit-rate assumptions.

Topics:
- Workload shape (prefix lengths, session vs ad-hoc)
- Batching tradeoffs: latency vs throughput
- KV cache architecture and hit-rate modelling
- Cost model assumptions and sensitivity (hit rate, batch size, seq len)
- Next steps: pilot & security docs

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan Lee from Redwood, AE on this. Priya is going to run through the Optimize recommendations, batching and the KV cache cost model, and then we'll save time for Q&A.
[00:28] Priya: Hi team, thanks Carlos, Emily, Rajiv. Quick agenda: first we recap the workload shape you shared, then dig into batching recommendations, go over KV / prefix caching options, and walk the cost spreadsheet with a few scenarios. I'll try to keep the math readable and we can pause any time.
[01:05] Carlos: Sounds good. Quick note we care most about customer-facing flows where the prefix is a 3-4 turn session, typical prefix tokens ~ 120-180, and ad-hoc queries are shorter. p95 latency target is 300ms for the short flows.
[02:01] Priya: Perfect, that helps. So two knobs we usually tune: batch size and prefix/KV cache. Batching improves GPU utilization — so if your qps has steady spikes, batching window of 8-16 is a sweet spot, gives 20-40% cost reduction in many of our tests. But larger batch size increases tail latency.
[03:10] Jordan: And just to be explicit, when we say "cost" in the model we mean GPU token cost + infra (redis/kv) amortized. We'll show a per-1M token baseline then apply cache hit-rate adjustments.
[04:12] Emily: How do you model the prefix cache hit rate? Our sessions vary a lot — some users repeat prompts, others are new.
[04:45] Priya: Great question. We generally split traffic into session-based hot prefixes and single-shot ad-hoc. For session-based we assume a hot set that hits at 40-70% depending on TTL and app behavior. In the spreadsheet scenario A we used 50% hit rate as a conservative baseline. We also include churn and cold-start penalty. Note, sometimes the transcripting system will show "KV cash" in notes, that's just a transcription quirk — it's KV cache.
[06:00] Rajiv: If hit rate drops to 20% the savings vanish right?
[06:18] Priya: It reduces them, yes. In the cost-model.xlsx we have a sensitivity tab. Example: baseline (no cache) cost = $120 per 1M tokens. With 50% prefix hit and batching 12, effective cost drops to ~$72 per 1M tokens in our example (rough numbers here). At 20% hit it's around $100 per 1M. So still some benefit from batching alone but the cache multiplies gains.
[08:12] Jordan: To add, the cache cost itself is small relative to GPU — a modest Redis cluster adds a few hundred dollars per month at pilot scale; the driver is the reduction in tokens served. We also support internal lightweight KV that runs co-located with inference instances if you want lower network egress and consistent latency.
[12:45] Emily: Can you walk the exact math for session flows? e.g., if a 4-turn session average prefix 150 tokens, and response length 60 tokens, what are we saving?
[13:10] Priya: Sure. Walkthrough: without cache you'd send full 150 tokens each request. If you have prefix cached, you only send delta tokens or use cached KV to skip re-encoding. So per request you'd save ~150 tokens. Over 4 turns that's 600 tokens saved per session. Multiply by qps and you get month estimate. In sheet: we also model KV cache warm cost — first time a prefix is cached you pay full cost. TTL affects amortization.
[20:10] Rajiv: There's also the question of model variants — quantized vs fp16 — and how that changes batching dynamics. How sensitive are these numbers?
[20:45] Priya: We include a model variant factor. For quantized int8 throughput increases and GPU cost per token drops 20-30% but sometimes at minor quality tradeoffs. The cost model has a toggle for quantized variants and adjusts kernel throughput accordingly. For many retrieval-augmented flows quantization is fine.
[27:30] Carlos: From a security standpoint, we need KMS integration and audit logs, and the ability to run private. Do you have a private deployment option for pilot?
[28:02] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and on-prem or VPC deployments. We'll share SOC2 + KMS integration docs in the follow-up (redwood-soc2.pdf link in the artifacts). For the pilot we suggested Hosted + dedicated capacity first for speed, then transition to Private if you need full network isolation.
[34:15] Emily: One implementation detail: eviction policies. We use user-level namespaces, can you do TTL per-namespace?
[34:40] Priya: Yes, TTL and per-namespace eviction policies are supported. You can tune TTL to the session length. Also the cache key shape matters — we recommend hashing normalized prefix + dialog state, avoid storing large raw text.
[41:50] Jordan: Quick live look — Priya, can you open the cost-model.xlsx and show the scenario tabs?
[42:05] Priya: Sure — Scenario A = conservative 50% hit, batching 12, quantized model -> delta ~40% cost reduction vs baseline. Scenario B = aggressive 70% hit -> ~55% savings. Scenario C = low hit 20% -> ~17% savings. I'll export these numbers and attach them after the call.
[45:10] Carlos: That's helpful. For next steps, we'll pull sample prefix distribution and get back to Redwood. Also want to run the 1-week pilot to validate hit rate.
[45:35] Jordan: Great. Recap of agreed next steps: Priya will send the spreadsheet and run an internal bench; Jordan will send pricing + pilot terms; Carlos will share prefix distributions and p95 targets. We'll aim to reconvene after the pilot kickoff. Thanks everyone.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription had a few swap words (e.g., "KV cash", "quantize" -> sometimes shown as "quant eyes"), we've manually corrected key items but left conversational bits as-is.

End of recording.
